messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: The two salts also had different brand names. Vistaril was the brand name for hydroxyzine pamoate, and Atarax was the brand name for hydroxyzine hydrochloride. Both brands have been discontinued in the United States, and hydroxyzine is now available as a generic medicine.
Is hydroxyzine pamoate stronger or longer lasting than hydroxyzine hydrochloride?:
No. You may read that hydroxyzine pamoate works better for anxiety, lasts longer, or reaches the brain more effectively than hydroxyzine hydrochloride. FDA-approved labeling does not support this.
Labeling for both salt forms states that hydroxyzine's effects are usually noticed within 15 to 30 minutes of a dose taken by mouth. Both are approved for the same three uses. Both carry the same doses, which are 50 to 100 mg four times a day for anxiety in adults, and 25 mg three or four times a day for itching. No FDA labeling describes a difference in how strongly or how long either form works.
Triples: [["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has brand name", "Vistaril"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has brand name", "Atarax"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has status", "discontinued in United States"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has status", "discontinued in United States"], ["hydroxyzine", "has availability", "generic medicine"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has effect onset", "15 to 30 minutes after oral dose"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has effect onset", "15 to 30 minutes after oral dose"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "approved for use in", "anxiety"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "approved for use in", "anxiety"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "approved for use in", "itching"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "approved for use in", "itching"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "approved for use in", "same three conditions as hydroxyzine hydrochloride"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "approved for use in", "same three conditions as hydroxyzine pamoate"], ["hydroxyzine", "has recommended dose for anxiety in adults", "50 to 100 mg four times a day"], ["hydroxyzine", "has recommended dose for itching", "25 mg three or four times a day"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has same dose as", "hydroxyzine hydrochloride"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has same dose as", "hydroxyzine pamoate"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "does not have stronger effect than", "hydroxyzine hydrochloride"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "does not have longer duration than", "hydroxyzine hydrochloride"], ["hydroxyzine", "has no difference in strength or duration between salt forms", "as per FDA labeling"]]
Relations: ["approved for use in", "does not have longer duration than", "does not have stronger effect than", "has availability", "has brand name", "has effect onset", "has no difference in strength or duration between salt forms", "has recommended dose for anxiety in adults", "has recommended dose for itching", "has same dose as", "has status"]
Answer:

completion:
has brand name: The subject compound is marketed under the brand name specified by the object entity.  
has status: The subject compound is no longer available or is discontinued in the specified region.  
has availability: The subject compound is available in the form of a generic medicine.  
has effect onset: The subject compound typically produces its effects within the time frame specified after oral administration.  
approved for use in: The subject compound is approved by regulatory authorities for treating the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
does not have longer duration than: The subject compound does not provide a prolonged duration of action compared to the compound specified by the object entity.  
does not have stronger effect than: The subject compound does not produce a more intense or potent effect compared to the compound specified by the object entity.  
has recommended dose for anxiety in adults: The subject compound is prescribed at the specified dose range for managing anxiety in adult patients.  
has recommended dose for itching: The subject compound is prescribed at the specified dose range for treating itching.  
has same dose as: The subject compound is prescribed at the same dose range as the compound specified by the object entity.  
has no difference in strength or duration between salt forms: As per official regulatory labeling, the subject compound and the specified compound have equivalent strength and duration of action.
